question: What is an ONTR refund and how do I apply for an MDA refund on the URA portal?
answer: An Other Non-Tax Revenue (ONTR) refund is a reimbursement for funds paid in error to a Ministry, Department, or Agency (MDA) through URA. To apply under the URA guide at https://ura.go.ug/en/tax-education/tax-refunds/: 1) Visit ura.go.ug and click on 'Get a Refund'; 2) Select 'Payment made to Ministry, Department or Agency (MDAs)' and click apply; 3) Enter the 13-digit Payment Registration Number (PRN) which auto-populates taxpayer details, along with email, mobile, and administrative location (district, county, subcounty, parish, village); 4) On the Refund Details page, enter the detailed reason for refund, commercial bank name, branch, account number, and account holder name (must match applicant name); 5) Upload required attachments (erroneous bank slip, correct bank slip, and letter from the MDA if available); 6) Enter the captcha and submit to receive an electronic acknowledgement receipt with an acknowledgement tracking number.

question: What is an NTR refund and how do I apply for a Motor Vehicle or Driving Permit refund?
answer: A Non-Tax Revenue (NTR) refund covers payments made in error for motor vehicle fees or driving permits. Under the URA guide at https://ura.go.ug/en/tax-education/tax-refunds/: 1) Go to ura.go.ug > Get a Refund > Motor vehicle or Driving permit; 2) Select the refund type (Motor vehicle: enter vehicle registration number plate; Driving permit: enter permit number); 3) Enter the refund amount, 13-digit PRN, mobile number, email, and address; 4) Under Refund Details, enter the detailed reason, commercial bank name, branch, account number, and account holder name (must match applicant name); 5) Note that because the portal currently has no online attachment upload field for NTRs, the claimant must submit copies of required attachments (erroneous/correct PRN, valid permit or transfer reference, NIN) to the nearest URA service centre or email them to services@ura.go.ug.

question: How do I apply for a Stamp Duty refund on the URA portal?
answer: To apply for a Stamp Duty refund: 1) Obtain a formal confirmation letter from the relevant MDA confirming that the service was not utilized; 2) Visit the Stamp Duty office or apply online for cancellation of the stamp duty instrument, attaching the MDA confirmation letter to receive an official cancellation notice with an assessment number; 3) Go to ura.go.ug > Get a Refund > Motor vehicle or Driving permit link > select Stamp Duty; 4) Select 'Refund For - Use Assessment Number' and enter the assessment number; 5) Enter bank details (commercial bank, branch, account number in applicant's name); 6) Submit required documents (cancellation notice with assessment number, stamp duty certificate with PRN, mobile number, and transaction documents) to the nearest URA office or email services@ura.go.ug.

question: What are the mandatory attachment requirements for claiming ONTR and NTR refunds?
answer: Under URA guidelines: 1) ONTR (MDAs): Erroneous/wrong/expired PRN and correct PRN, NIN for individuals, passport/work permit for foreign nationals, TIN/URSB registration for companies, bank account details in applicant/company name, birth certificate and parent ID for minors, court documents/confirmation for Judiciary, letter of administration for deceased, and MDA confirmation letter; 2) NTR Driving Permits: Erroneous/correct PRN, valid driving permit, NIN, mobile number, bank account details, and Police letter for duplicate permits; 3) NTR Motor Vehicle: Erroneous/correct PRN, number plate, TIN/NIN, motor vehicle transfer application reference number, mobile number, and bank account details; 4) Stamp Duty: Stamp duty cancellation notice with assessment number, stamp duty certificate with PRN, mobile number, and transaction agreements.

question: What are common mistakes to avoid when applying for a URA tax refund?
answer: Common errors that delay or invalidate refund claims include: 1) Missing mobile telephone number at payment registration and refund application; 2) Bank account name differing from the name registered on the PRN; 3) Failure to provide both the erroneous PRN and the correct new PRN; 4) Failing to attach copy of driving permit for permit refunds; 5) Providing non-commercial bank accounts; 6) Not obtaining an official cancellation notice with assessment number before applying for stamp duty refunds.
